dialogue.Introduction: Oh, a new face. I'm the Nurse, and no, I don't take complaints as payment. I take coins. Are you bleeding?$h
dialogue.Mon: The clinic opens early on Mondays, mostly so the miners can get stitched before the mines swallow them whole.
dialogue.Tue: Tuesday. Fresh linens, fresh bandages, and somehow the same old scrapes from the same old fools.
dialogue.Wed: Hello, @. The kitchen smells of coffee, which means I have been awake since before the rooster.
dialogue.Thu: Some folk say the valley is quiet. I say quiet is what people call a place just before the slimes arrive.$u
dialogue.Fri: Friday. Nobody gets sick on a Friday, which is suspicious. Someone is faking it to dodge farm work, and I have a good guess who.
dialogue.Sat: Market day. The Merchant is shouting about bandage prices again. I'd shout back too, if I were not so tired.$h
dialogue.Sun: Sundays I rest. Well, I try. Then someone falls off the mountain and I'm back at it by noon.
dialogue.Mon2: Oh, you again. Good. Better you than the Demolitionist, who keeps asking if my cabinets would make a fine bonfire.$h
dialogue.Wed6: You have good instincts, @. I keep a private list of the people I never have to stitch twice. You are on it.$h
dialogue.Fri10: I save the good bandages for people I would lose sleep over, @. I am starting to run out of good bandages.$l
dialogue.Sun2: The sun is lovely on the clinic porch. Would you believe I have never sat out there? Not once in two years.$s
dialogue.Mon4: Mondays are my favourite. Nobody has taken a bad turn yet this week, and I like starting with a clean slate.$h
dialogue.Tue4: I keep a notebook of every patient in the valley. Yours has more doodles than notes. Oh, don't be embarrassed.$h
dialogue.Wed4: Coffee and a sunny window. That is my idea of a nice morning, and it is better when you walk in with a grin.$h
dialogue.Thu4: My mother was a healer too, in a town far from here. She used to say a bandage is only as good as the hand that ties it.$h
dialogue.Fri4: Fridays feel longer when I can't stop thinking about the clinic. Not the job, you understand. The people.$h
dialogue.Sat4: I have been saving a seat for you by the window. Don't tell the cat, he gets jealous.$h
dialogue.Sun4: Sunday is quiet enough to think. I used to think about old scars. Now I think about who I would like to visit.$h
dialogue.Mon8: @, I am glad you came in today. Sometimes I let my tea go cold just to wait for the bell over the door.$l
dialogue.Tue8: I have never told anyone that I was afraid of the dark mines when I was small. Now I stand guard at their mouths with a roll of bandage.$s
dialogue.Wed8: When the blood moon rises, I lie awake wondering who I will be patching up. I would rather it was you than a stranger.$l
dialogue.Thu8: I used to think this job was about wounds. It is really about the people who come back. You keep coming back, @.$l
dialogue.Fri8: Be honest with me. Do you ever sleep? You look like you walked back from the Skull Cavern on pure stubbornness.$h
dialogue.Sat8: I will confess something. I wrote your name on the clinic chart, next to the words do not let escape. The ink is a bit smudged now.$l
dialogue.Sun8: Stay for supper tonight? I will probably burn the soup, but the company will be good, and that is the only medicine I trust.$l
dialogue.danceRejection: Dance with you at the Flower Dance? I would need a few more hearts and a much sturdier pair of shoes first.$u
dialogue.summer_Wed: Summer heat makes the slimes nasty and the patients nastier. Bring water, will you? A bucket. A big one.$a
dialogue.winter_Fri8: Winter nights make the clinic feel like a little boat. Stay a minute, @, and tell me something that is not a broken bone.$l
dialogue.fall_Fri: Fall sends the leaves down and the complaints up. It is a fine time to be stubborn about rest, I have decided.$h
dialogue.spring_Sat4: I always think spring is for wounds that finally heal. It is the one season I do not mind getting sap on my hands.$h
dialogue.fall_15: Halfway through fall and I am out of Lesser Healing potions again. You would think folks would learn.$a
dialogue.winter_20: Cold hands make bad stitches. So I have taken up knitting, and so far the bandages look like a blanket.$h
dialogue.spring_9: Spring rain turns the paths to mud and my patients arrive soggy. I have started a waiting list. You are at the top, naturally.$h
dialogue.summer_Tue6: You pulled me off the mountain path yesterday, @. I wanted to thank you properly, so here is a free tonic. Don't ask what is in it.$h
dialogue.winter_Mon: Monday. Quiet clinic, warm cocoa. I could get used to a day like this, if I let myself.$h
dialogue.spring_Thu8: I went out to the fields to pick herbs for you. No, I went for herbs for me. Stop smiling at me like that.$l
dialogue.summer_Sun10: A walk on the beach? Don't look at me like I'm about to say yes. I'm about to say I'll think about it. Maybe after a swim.$l
dialogue.fall_Sat2: The fair is on, and the first-aid booth is the only one with no line. I wonder why that is.$h
dialogue.winter_Wed4: Most people only visit the clinic when they are hurt. You come when you are bored. I am noticing.$h
dialogue.spring_3: Early spring, and the first patient was the one who tried to tame a bunny with a pickaxe.$h
dialogue.summer_12: Festival season is fine. Only fools get hurt, and most of the fools in this valley are my favourite people.$h

rainy: Rain again. The clinic smells of wet dog and wet bandages, and I have decided that is a fine smell for healing.$h

marriage.Indoor_Day_0: Good morning, @. The kettle is on, and you look like you slept in a cave again.$h
marriage.Indoor_Day_1: The house is warm today. I like that more than I thought I would.$h
marriage.Indoor_Day_2: Could you pass the thread? I am patching the blanket. The cat thinks the thread is a toy.$h
marriage.Indoor_Day_3: I have written a list of chores for us. It is long. Start with the dishes, love.$h
marriage.Indoor_Day_4: I have been thinking about the clinic. One day we might have a proper kitchen table instead of a bed full of bandages.$l
marriage.Rainy_Day_0: Rain on the roof and you on the couch. Should I be worried or delighted? Delighted, I think.$h
marriage.Rainy_Day_1: It is raining again. Perfect for mending socks and not going outside, which I am told is a crime in this valley.$h
marriage.Rainy_Day_2: Muddy boots at the door again, @. Take them off before you track mud through the clinic. Oh. It is our house now.$h
marriage.Rainy_Day_3: Listen to the rain. It sounds like a patient finally going to sleep.$h
marriage.Rainy_Day_4: Rainy mornings are when I miss the sun least, mostly because you are here, and that is warmer.$l
marriage.Indoor_Night_0: It is late, @. Come to bed before the moon gets bored of us.$h
marriage.Indoor_Night_1: I was reading in the chair. The book was dull, so I watched you sleep instead. Don't be smug about it.$l
marriage.Indoor_Night_2: Turn the lamp down, please. My eyes are tired from counting bandages in the dark.$h
marriage.Indoor_Night_3: Did you lock the door? Good. The mines have been noisy lately, and I sleep better when the house is safe.$h
marriage.Indoor_Night_4: Goodnight, @. I will be the one snoring. Blame the cat, he is on my chest again.$h
marriage.Rainy_Night_0: Rain on the window at night. It is hard to sleep when I keep thinking of everyone we have healed.$s
marriage.Rainy_Night_1: Hear that thunder? Scoot closer. The slimes always get braver in a storm, and so do I.$h
marriage.Rainy_Night_2: I can't sleep with the rain this loud. Stay here until it stops, please, love.$l
marriage.Rainy_Night_3: Our house sounds like a drum tonight. I would call it cosy if I were a cat.$h
marriage.Rainy_Night_4: Goodnight in the rain. Strange how much I like it when you are beside me.$l
marriage.Outdoor_0: Out here with you, the valley looks softer. Even the grass seems to lean closer.$h
marriage.Outdoor_1: Shall we walk along the river? I will bring the bandages, in case you fall in the water again.$h
marriage.Outdoor_2: Careful on the path, @. You know what my job is. I would rather not spend my day off cleaning up after you.$h
marriage.Outdoor_3: The sky is so clear today. I had forgotten how big it is when I am not staring at clinic ceilings.$h
marriage.Outdoor_4: Let's sit here a minute. The crops are doing fine, and so are we. That is enough for one whole day.$l
marriage.Good_0: You have made my whole morning, @. Truly.$h
marriage.Good_1: Thank you for the flowers. I put them in the clinic window where the patients can see them.$h
marriage.Good_2: Look at that, the grass is greening, and I am green with envy over your garden.$h
marriage.Good_3: Today feels light. Maybe the clinic will stay quiet for a whole afternoon.$h
marriage.Good_4: I would like to take a day off with you. Just one. We will see if I keep my promise.$h
marriage.Good_5: The valley is good today, and so are you. My blood pressure agrees.$l
marriage.Good_6: Sunshine, a good meal, and you back from the mines in one piece. What a day.$h
marriage.Good_7: Honestly, you make a bad mood look silly. Keep doing that.$h
marriage.Good_8: I love the way you hum when you chop wood. It is terrible and I adore it.$l
marriage.Good_9: I am proud of you, @. Quietly, the way I am proud of a clean stitch.$l
marriage.Neutral_1: It is an ordinary day. Ordinary is fine with me.
marriage.Neutral_2: Hmm? Oh, I was miles away. The clinic ledger is a mess.
marriage.Neutral_3: Could you put the kettle on? I am not moving until I finish this chart.
marriage.Neutral_4: Another letter from the Merchant about bandage prices. I'll read it later.
marriage.Neutral_5: The cat knocked over the tea again. He is not sorry, and neither am I.
marriage.Neutral_6: It is an all right day, @. Mostly bandages and quiet.
marriage.Neutral_7: Did you remember the chicken feed? I cannot recall a single thing today.
marriage.Neutral_8: You have a leaf in your hair. Don't ask me how it got there. I wasn't looking.
marriage.Neutral_9: Let's leave the dishes for later. Tonight I want the sofa and nothing else.
marriage.Bad_0: Don't talk to me before breakfast. I am very short today, @.$a
marriage.Bad_1: I have had enough blood and bruises for one week. Please, just be quiet for a bit.$a
marriage.Bad_2: You tracked mud through the hall again. The mop is in the corner. You know where it is.$a
marriage.Bad_3: I am tired, and it is your fault for being so cheerful. Go away for an hour, will you?$a
marriage.Bad_4: I asked you for one thing. One. The lamp was still on this morning.$a
marriage.Bad_5: Please don't make jokes right now. The clinic lost a patient and I am not in the mood.$s
marriage.Bad_6: You are standing there like a statue. Say something useful or go outside.$a
marriage.Bad_7: I bought the wrong kind of thread and I am furious. It is not your fault. It is a little bit your fault.$a
marriage.Bad_8: We are not discussing the broken cup today. I have decided that.$a
marriage.Bad_9: Just leave me alone, @. I will apologise over supper.$s
marriage.OneKid_0: %kid1 fell off the porch again. I have the bandages out, @. She says she is fine, and she is crying in the other room.$h
marriage.OneKid_1: %kid1 asked me if slimes have mothers. I said yes, and they are worse than mine.$h
marriage.OneKid_2: Our child is growing so fast, @. Remember when I had to hold them with two hands? Now they run to the clinic grinning.$h
marriage.OneKid_3: Look at %kid1 trying to stitch a teddy bear. The patient will need a bandage too.$h
marriage.TwoKids_0: %kid1 and %kid2 have finally stopped fighting over the blanket. For now. I am enjoying the peace.$h
marriage.TwoKids_1: Two kids and one kitchen table. I would like a bigger table, love, and maybe a bigger bed.$h
marriage.TwoKids_2: %kid2 wants to be a doctor like me, and %kid1 wants to be a goblin. I am trying to stay out of the middle.$h
marriage.TwoKids_3: The house is full of noise, @, and I have never been happier. Don't let anyone tell you I am soft.$h
marriage.NoBed_0: There is no spare bed, so you will have to sleep on the sofa. Don't complain. The sofa is my favourite place to nap.$h
marriage.NoBed_1: The bed is still unmade and the guest room is full of bandages. The sofa will do.$h
marriage.NoBed_2: I am sorry, there is no spare bed. I will bring you a blanket, and we will call it a sleepover.$h
marriage.NoBed_3: Shh. Don't wake the cat, @. He has taken the last warm spot on the sofa.$h
marriage.patio_Harvey: Lovely day for the patio, @. Let's sit with our tea and watch the valley bustle.$h
marriage.spouseRoom_Harvey: Our room is the best room in the house. Sunshine, a window and you, @. What more could a nurse ask for?$l
marriage.funLeave_Harvey: I am off to the clinic for the morning, love. Don't burn the toast while I am gone.$h
marriage.funReturn_Harvey: I am home, @! Missed me? Don't answer, I can tell from your face.$h
marriage.Outdoor_Harvey: I took a walk outside today. Fresh air did me more good than any potion I could brew.$h
marriage.spring_Harvey: Blossoms everywhere, and I can finally open the clinic windows. Wonderful for the patients and the flowers.$h
marriage.summer_Harvey: The summer heat has made me lazy. The only thing I want to do is lie in the grass with you.$l
marriage.fall_Harvey: The leaves are turning and the clinic has gone quiet at last. I would like to spend some of that quiet with you.$h
marriage.winter_Harvey: Winter keeps the patients indoors and me by the fire with you, @. I am not complaining one bit.$h

situations.eye: The Eye of Cthulhu is gone? Good riddance. I have stitched up guards for less. Rest up, @.$h
situations.evilBoss: The Eater of Worlds or the Brain of Cthulhu is down, and I have put the sad little bandages away for now. Take a breath, friend.$h
situations.skeletron: Skeletron fell and the dungeon is open, and the Old Man is free. That means the clinic will see bone trouble again.$s
situations.queenBee: The Queen Bee is down. Honey everywhere, and every stinger I pulled from someone's arm was a tiny miracle.$h
situations.hardmode: The Wall of Flesh is gone and hardmode has begun. The Hallow is spreading and so are the monsters. Please be careful out there.$s
situations.mechs: A mechanical boss was destroyed. The wreckage was sharp. I am putting a tetanus shot on the chart for everyone.$a
situations.plantera: Plantera fell and the jungle temple is open. I would love to see the plants, but I would rather see them without thorns in my hands.$h
situations.golem: The Golem is in pieces. Nice work. I have been brushing stone dust out of my hair for days, but it was worth it.$h
situations.cultist: The Lunatic Cultist is defeated and the pillars have appeared in the sky. I stared at them so long I forgot to eat.$u
situations.moonLord: The Moon Lord fell and the sky has calmed. I want to sleep for three days, and then I would like a parade. Both, please.$h
situations.goblins: The goblin army has been repelled. Every goblin with a bump on the head was a welcome patient. Good work, @.$h
situations.pirates: The pirates are gone, leaving only sand in the clinic. My broom has never worked this hard in its life.$a
situations.frostLegion: The Frost Legion is beaten. The frozen soldiers were easier to stitch than you would think.$h
situations.martians: The Martians went home, or at least away. Their ray guns made quite a mess of my tables. Please stop asking why I am grumbling.$a
situations.bloodMoon: There was a blood moon last night. The clinic filled with people who swore the moon whispered to them. I told them all to go to bed.$s
situations.eclipse: The solar eclipse was lovely, and the sudden dark sent three people to my door with headaches. Next time, wear a proper hat and stop staring at the sky.$h
situations.party: The Party Girl is throwing a party today. Please don't drink the punch. I have stitched up more party guests than I would like to admit.$h

festivals.spring13: Egg Festival! I am handing out dyed eggs to the kids and bandages to the ones who tried to eat them.$h
festivals.spring24: The Flower Dance. Half the valley wants to dance and the other half wants me to patch them up after.$h
festivals.summer11: Luau day! I will add a healing herb to the soup, just a pinch. The Dryad cannot tell and neither can you.$h
festivals.summer28: The jellies rise tonight. Lovely, glowing, and every one of them stings like a wasp. Keep your sleeves down.$h
festivals.fall16: Fair day! I am running the first-aid booth. The Pirate says it is pointless, but he had his arm sewn up last week.$h
festivals.fall27: Spirit's Eve, and the maze is full of things that go bump. Don't worry, I would sooner stitch up a ghost than fear one.$h
festivals.winter8: Ice fishing! Half the valley will fall in the lake, and I will be the one with the warm blanket. Bring your own socks.$h
festivals.winter25: Winter Star! Here is a small gift for you. Don't open it near the clinic. It might be a bandage.$h
festivals.spring13_spouse: Dyed eggs again, @. I did mine in the shape of little bandages. Our kids will find them and be horrified.$h
festivals.spring24_spouse: The Flower Dance with you, @. I tripped on the first step and you caught me. I am not complaining.$l
festivals.summer11_spouse: We put our soup in the pot together, @. Ours is the only one with a dash of healing and a dash of love.$l
festivals.summer28_spouse: Jellies on the beach with you. Stay close, love. The glow makes it hard to tell whether you are hurt.$l
festivals.fall16_spouse: The fair with you makes everything fun. The first-aid booth is quiet, so we get to sit and talk.$h
festivals.fall27_spouse: Spirit's Eve with you is a treat. You take the maze and I take the candy, and we swap at the gate.$h
festivals.winter8_spouse: Ice fishing, and you are still in the water up to your knees. Get out here before you catch a cold.$a
festivals.winter25_spouse: Our first Winter Star together, @. A little kit with bandages, tea and a note saying you are worth stitching up.$l

loved.text: Coffee and honey? You know exactly what a nurse needs. Thank you, @. I will drink it while I stitch.$h

liked.text: Wildflowers! They will brighten the clinic window. You are thinking like a healer, @.$h

neutral.text: Oh. Thanks, I suppose. Put it on the shelf by the door, next to the other odd things.

disliked.text: Bombs! Dynamite! Do you want me to be sick? Take it back before someone ends up in my bed.$a

hated.text: A gun? In my clinic? Take that away this minute, @. I will not have one more bullet hole in this house.$a

help: Someone hold that slime off my bandages, now!
I cannot heal and fight at once, so bring help!
Hold the line! Bring me the hurt, I will patch them!
thanks: Good hands, @, and good timing. I am not dead yet, so that is a win.$h
You kept my clinic standing and my patients breathing, @. Thank you.$l
battle: Back off, you little menace. I have stitched worse!
You want a fight? Fine. I have a needle for you!
Hold still! This will sting, and it is your fault!
I do not run from slimes. I just stitch them up!
courage.hurt: I took a slime to the shin, which is a fine way to learn humility. Rest is an order, and I am giving it to myself.$a

danger.boss: A boss is loose and my bandage roll is ready. Keep your head down, @, and come to me if you bleed.$h
danger.invasion: An army is marching on the valley. Kettle is on, bandages are out, and I am not leaving my post.$h
danger.pumpkinMoon: The Pumpkin Moon is up and the scarecrows are restless. I will heal anyone who holds the line.$h
danger.frostMoon: Frost Moon. Cold hands make bad stitches, so I am bundled up and ready for the frost legion.$h
danger.eclipse: The sun has gone dark and the eclipse monsters are about. I am staying at my post with the lamp lit.$h
danger.bloodMoon: The blood moon is high. Every wound tonight will need me, so I am staying close to the door.$s

events.after: Keep your bandages dry and stay out of the mine carts, will you?

steps.say: Oh, it is @. Come in, come in, and mind the bandage rolls on the floor. Nobody has tidied since the slime incident.$u

You look like a goblin tried to ride you down the mine cart. Sit. Hold still. This will sting. Mostly my pride, when I say it.#$b#Scrapes from the mines pay my rent, so I suppose I should thank you for the custom.$h

steps.question: Do you always go down the mines without a helmet?

answers.reply: Tuesdays. Right. I will put that on your chart, shall I?$a
Cowards are the ones who live long enough to be bored. Wear the helmet.$a

steps.say: Right. Three lesser healing potions. Drink one before you need it, not after, because nothing I brew can fix a crushed skull.$h
Now off with you. The bus stop does not need your blood on the bench.$h

events.after: The Merchant wants you to buy his special bandage. I told him to take a long walk off a short pier.$a

steps.say: @! Oh thank goodness, you can help me. The Merchant has been trying to sell me a bandage at three times its price.$a
Three times? Friend, that is a bargain! Each bandage comes with the healing feeling included.$h
The healing feeling is mostly a cactus rubbing on your arm. I have seen it.$h
Hmm! Then perhaps a discount for the clinic. Two bandages for the price of one, and I throw in a smile.$h

steps.question: Should we take the Merchant up on his deal?

answers.text: Yes, the Merchant needs the coin.
answers.reply: Look at that, a kind soul. Possibly a fool, but a kind one.$h

answers.text: No, let him sell to the slimes.
answers.reply: Slimes do not carry coins. Unfortunately for everybody.$a

steps.say: Right, enough. The Merchant may sell whatever he likes. I am on my lunch break, eating a sandwich in the sun.$h
Excuse me! I have a shop to sell from and a bell to ring!$h

events.after: If you come by tomorrow, I might even tell you about the cactus incident.$h

steps.say: Oh. You are still awake, @? So am I. The clinic is so quiet at night I can hear the slimes thinking.$u

Did you know I was not always a nurse? I was a frightened apprentice who once fainted at the sight of a single drop of blood.#$b#My old teacher pinched my ear and said a healer who faints is just a patient with better hair.$h
I have always been afraid of being useless, @. Not of blood. Blood is only paint, once you stop looking at it.$s

steps.question: Are you ever afraid of the valley?

answers.reply: Then we are the same sort of fool. Good. Fools stick together.$h

answers.text: Not really, I have good friends.
answers.reply: Lucky you. I am glad you have friends who keep you safe.$h

steps.say: I came to Pelican Town to forget the bad days. Somehow I keep finding the good ones here.$h
Go on home and sleep. The clinic will still be here in the morning, and so will I.$h

events.after: Tomorrow, the teapot. Don't be late, I have a plan for the chipped cup.$h

steps.say: @? You came by after hours. I thought the clinic was locked, but I see I have been leaving the door open for you.$l
I have been trying to find the right words for a week. Every time I open my mouth, I end up talking about bandages.$s
You make me want to stay up later than my patients. I do not know if that is a healthy sign, but I like it.$l

steps.question: Would you like to have tea with me tomorrow?

answers.reply: Good. Bring your own cup. Mine is chipped, like my heart. Just a little.$l
Fine, next week. I will keep the kettle warm and my patience cold.$s

steps.say: I need to tell you something honest, @. I am glad it was you who walked in with a scraped knee that first day.$l
Now go home before I stitch you to the chair so you cannot leave.$h

events.after: I have been humming all day, which my patients find quite alarming.$l

steps.say: Oh, @. You found me on the beach. I came out to look at the stars, but the stars look a lot like you right now.$l
I come down here because the waves calm me. Funny, really. As a nurse, the waves have never once asked me for a bandage.$h

steps.question: Do you come down here often?

answers.reply: Oh, that is cheap, but I believe you. My heart is doing that thing again.$l

answers.text: Every night, since you moved in.
answers.reply: Every night? Then I am the one keeping you up. Oh dear. How lovely.$h

steps.say: Can I tell you something I have never told anybody? I think about you when I am stitching, and I forget which thread I was holding.$l
Dance with me? The waves are the only music I can hear, but I think it will do.$h

events.after: Sit with me a while longer, love. The clinic can wait until morning.$l

steps.say: Tea is ready, @. I made it the way you like it. Less honey, more of my patience.$l
Do you remember the first day you came into the clinic? You had a scraped knee and a grin like a cat with a fish.$h
I thought you were trouble. You are, but you are my trouble now, and I would not trade it for any cure in the valley.$l

steps.question: Shall we raise a few kids in this house?

answers.reply: Oh, you are impossible. I will need a much bigger bed first.$h
Fine. Festivals first, then the messy business. I will get the cradle ready.$h

steps.say: Now drink your tea before it gets cold. I will not have you ruin it with that stubborn face.$h
Good. Now sit beside me, love. The clinic can wait until morning.$l
